questions.text:
In cryptography, the following uses transposition ciphers and the keyword is LAYER. Encrypt the following message. (Spaces are omitted during encrypton)
WELCOME TO NETWORK SECURITY!
questions.solution:
Write WELCOMETONETWORKSECURITY! in rows of 5 under L A Y E R:
WELCO / METON / ETWOR / KSECU / RITY!

Read the columns in alphabetical order of the key letters (A, E, L, R, Y):
A: EETSI, E: COOCY, L: WMEKR, R: ONRU!, Y: LTWET

Answer: EETSICOOCYWMEKRONRU!LTWET

questions.text: Assuming that for a given network layer implementation, connection establishment overhead is 100 bytes and disconnection overhead is 28 bytes. What would be the minimum size of the packet the transport layer needs to keep up, if it wishes to implement a datagram service above the network layer and needs to keep its overhead to a minimum of 12.5%. (ignore transport layer overhead)
questions.solution:
Each datagram pays for connection setup and teardown: 100 + 28 = 128 bytes. For this to be at most 12.5% of the packet:
[latex]128\le0.125\times P\Rightarrow P\ge1024[/latex] bytes

Answer: 1024 bytes

questions.text: StationA uses 32 byte packets to transmit messages to Station B using a sliding window protocol. The round trip delay between A and B is 80 ms and the bottleneck bandwidth on the path between A and B is 128 kbps. What is the optimal window size that A should use?
questions.solution:
To keep the pipe full, the window must cover bandwidth [latex]\times[/latex] RTT:
[latex]128\times10^3\times80\times10^{-3}=10240[/latex] bits = 1280 bytes.

Packets = 1280 / 32 = 40

Answer: 40

questions.text: ________ can detect burst error of length less than or equal to degree of the polynomial and detects burst errors that affect odd number of bits.
questions.solution:
A CRC with a degree-r generator detects all burst errors of length [latex]\le r[/latex], and (with a factor x + 1) all errors affecting an odd number of bits.

Answer: CRC
